title: Remote Access Trojans (RATs) | Major RAT Families, How They Work and How to Detect Them
content_md: What Is a Remote Access Trojan (RAT)? A remote access trojan (RAT) is malware that gives an attacker hidden, interactive control over someone else’s computer. Once it runs, the operator can see the screen, read files, record keystrokes, and issue commands as if they were sitting at the keyboard. RATs are also a staple of botnet infrastructure: the Spamhaus Project found they accounted for 42% of the Top 20 malware families associated with botnet command-and-control activity in the second half of 2025. Remote access trojan definition in plain English A remote access trojan is a malicious program that quietly hands a stranger remote control of your device. It is a trojan because it arrives disguised as something harmless, such as an invoice, a cracked game, or a software installer. It is a remote access tool because, once it runs, the attacker can connect from anywhere and operate the machine. The victim usually sees nothing unusual, which is why RATs are used for long-running surveillance as well as quick theft.
